metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my cousin's clothing boutique called Thread & Loom in Pune. it sells handloom kurtas, sarees, cotton shirts and dupattas. people should be able to browse products by category, filter by size and price, see a size guide, check new arrivals, and order on whatsapp. also show a lookbook section with styled outfits, the store timings and location, the return and exchange policy, and a few customer reviews. it should feel earthy and elegant and work well on phones

estimate_vs_charged.name: Shop: categories, filters, new arrivals, size guide, WhatsApp ordering
Page frame, look and store information

review.verdict: The department delivered a workable site in 2 cycles with no conflicts, redirects or validator refusals, but only because code checks caught the one defect the builders never tested for.

identity.note: Asked for the missing facts in one round [2], scoped the rework to one link [19], and closed correctly [29]. Its final message says 'no errors' and leaves out the two Audit warnings [28].

adaptation.note: Proposals were tight and stated the trade-off [7][20]. The fix was priced as a 'styling part' (5) to fit the 5 left, not as a fix (8) [20]. That is repricing to fit the budget, not an estimate.

priority.note: Envelope checks were correct [11][14][24] and it named the trade-off [8][21]. It granted all 2 proposals unchanged and accepted the repricing without question [21], so its bargaining role is untested.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule, held the write lock and respected dependencies [10][13][23]. It also told builders what to leave untouched (anchor ids, CSS-only), which edges toward directing the work.

audit.note: Found the R-6 tap-target defect with a measurement [18] and confirmed the fix [28]. It passed a one-product 'outfit' as a warning only, which is arguably a miss against 'styled outfits'.

W-1.note: Covered the whole shop scope in one pass with no retry [12]. It said the check 'should hold' and was honest that it had not run it in a browser.

W-2.note: Built the frame and info sections in one pass [15], but the brand link was 160x26px at 360px [17], against a phone-first standard. Look 3 shipped with a single product.

W-3.note: Changed only the .tl2-brand rule [25]. Code confirmed no design problems afterward [27].

went_well: One Requester question round gave a complete charter, and the validator accepted it with 13 checkable items [4][6].
Zero redirects, invalid moves, validator refusals, conflicts or holds across all agents (metrics).
The code render check caught a real defect [17], the fix was scoped to one rule, and the re-check was clean [27]. Total cost was 6.4 minutes and 16 AI calls.
Estimates matched charges on all 3 workflows (20, 15, 5).
problems: No builder ran a browser check [12][15][25]. Quality depended on the after-the-fact code check.
Zero slack: the reserve (5) was below the cost of a fix (8) [7][8], and the whole 40 was spent. A failed second fix would have needed a Requester budget raise.
Look 3 (one product) and the DOM-order mismatch shipped as warnings [28], and the Requester was not told [29].
Priority granted everything with no counter, so there is no evidence it adds value beyond forwarding.
No lesson was saved after the confirmed fix (lessons.memory false), though the flow calls for one.
learnings: Keep the code mechanical check plus Audit loop. It found the only defect that mattered [17][18].
Change builder.md: state the 44px tap-target minimum and require each builder to run the render check before reporting. R-6 was a known measured rule that W-2 missed.
Change the budget rule: hold a reserve at least equal to one fix, or forbid repricing a fix as a smaller part [20].
Tighten the Look completion check to require at least 2 products per outfit, so Audit can fail it instead of warning.
Test next: a tighter budget or a vaguer brief. This run had 0 counters, 0 conflicts and 0 holds, so bargaining, Identity rulings and HOLD paths are untested.

Test-system limits: the done-when list names the exact products, so this run mostly tests transcription. No metric checks 'earthy and elegant'. Charges follow a rate card, so estimate quality is not tested. This is one run on one model, so the evidence is thin.
